sections.h2: Which Miami office sends the tax bill, and which one sets the value?
sections.html:
Two county offices split the work. The Miami-Dade Tax Collector mails and collects the bill, and the Property Appraiser of Miami-Dade County sets the values the bill is built from. The appraiser's home page says outright that it does not send bills, set taxes or collect them.

The city of Miami adds its own mills to the same statement, alongside county, school and special district lines. The city covers 36.00 square miles and held about 489,812 residents in mid-2025, up 10.8 percent from the 2020 base, so two parcels in different neighborhoods can sit on different taxing lines.

  • Appraiser, main office: Stephen P. Clark Center, 111 NW 1st Street, Suite 710, Monday to Friday 8 to 5, phone 305-375-4712.
  • Appraiser, southern branch: South Dade Government Center, 10710 SW 211 Street, Cutler Bay, 305-232-3810.
  • Tax Collector: pays online around the clock, through 13 locations and via mobile T-Connect offices, according to its home page.

sections.h2: What millage does the county's 2026 chart assign to Miami?
sections.html:
Miami's city operating levy is 7.1080 mills, with 0.2536 more for city debt service, and every authority together totals 19.9544 mills. The county prints the chart under the title 2026 adopted millage rates.

A separate row for the downtown development area adds 0.3800 and totals 20.3344. A house inside that boundary uses the second figure, so confirm the row from the appraiser's parcel search. One mill equals one dollar of tax per thousand dollars of taxable value.

The city line alone is larger than Coral Gables at 5.5590 and Miami Beach at 5.8060.

sections.h2: How do Miami's total mills compare with neighboring cities?
sections.html:
Miami's 19.9544 beats Coral Gables at 18.1518, Hialeah at 18.6134 and Miami Beach at 18.6681, and trails North Miami at 22.1081 and Miami Gardens at 22.3393.

sections.h2: What kind of city is Miami, and who lives in its houses?
sections.html:
The Census counted 442,241 people in 2020, up from 399,457 in 2010, at 12,285.8 residents per square mile. Foreign-born residents make up 57.7 percent, 7,305 are veterans, and the average commute is 27.3 minutes. Among adults 25 and older, 81.3 percent finished high school and 37.4 percent hold a four-year degree.

The 2022 business census lists about $17.0 billion in transportation and warehousing receipts, $13.2 billion in retail sales and $8.7 billion in health care revenue.

Only 30.8 percent of housing units are owner occupied. The city counts 194,821 households, a median owner-reported home value of $518,100, median gross rent of $1,758, median household income of $62,462 in 2024 dollars and a 19.4 percent poverty rate. In a renter-heavy city, many houses belong to investors, and an investor selling a Miami house usually has no homestead relief to lose.

sections.h2: Which Miami-Dade tax milestones came in 2026?
sections.html:
The appraiser's home page gives the county's own sequence for the 2026 roll.

  • June 1 estimate: countywide taxable value of $540.7 billion, up 5.5 percent from 2025, which is 3.2 percentage points slower than the prior year's growth.
  • September 1: the Board of County Commissioners ordered the tax rolls extended.
  • October 16: the appraiser certified the roll, before any Value Adjustment Board changes.
  • November to February: the discount months, which the Tax Collector promotes as a chance to save 4 percent by paying in November.
  • April 1: unpaid bills are delinquent.

The appraiser's site also offers a property tax estimator tutorial showing how the Amendment 3 changes would work out for 2027 and 2028.

sections.h2: What should a Miami seller collect before the closing table?
sections.html:
Gather the folio number, the August TRIM notice with its proposed taxes, proof of every exemption on file and a payoff letter from the Tax Collector if any year is open.

Widow(er) and veteran disability exemptions can now be filed online through the appraiser's exemptions tool, and agricultural classification applications on Form MD-482 can be filed online too. A house inside the downtown development area needs the title agent's attention, because it carries the extra 0.3800 mills. Buyers should expect the first bill after purchase to start from just value, which can run well above the seller's bill.

sections.h2: How does a Miami owner claim homestead or move the Save Our Homes benefit?
sections.html:
File Form DR-501 with the appraiser by March 1, and make the home your permanent residence by January 1. A rented house loses the exemption. The state's yearly growth limit is the lower of 3 percent or inflation.

When you buy another Florida home, portability can carry your assessment savings along if the new homestead starts within three years, with Form DR-501T filed with the DR-501. A suspected abuse of homestead can be reported to the appraiser's compliance unit at 305-375-3402.

For a bill that is hard to pay, deferral requests (Form DR-570) are due March 31 and installment requests May 1.

sections.h2: What if back taxes are owed on a Miami house?
sections.html:
An unpaid bill becomes delinquent on April 1, and the Tax Collector sells a certificate against it by June 1. The certificate holder cannot demand money from the owner for two years after April 1 of the issue year. A deed application costs $75, and on a homestead the opening bid adds half of the latest assessed value.

A seller with arrears can still close, because the title company pays the lien from proceeds. Ask for the payoff figure early.

sections.h2: What does a Miami tax deed auction involve?
sections.html:
If a certificate stays unpaid, the clerk can hold a public auction. The top bidder posts a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is larger. The Tax Collector lists who must be notified: the titleholder, lienholders, mortgagees and contract-for-deed vendees.

With no bidder, the property goes on a list of lands available for taxes, and the county has 90 days to buy it at the opening bid. An owner who is behind should call the Tax Collector long before an auction is scheduled.

At the Miami-Dade County Recorder's Office, 20 NW 1st Avenue, Suite 5.246, run by the county clerk. The clerk's checklist asks for the seller's original signature, two unrelated witnesses with printed names and addresses, a notary acknowledgement and a Prepared By line. Deed stamps run 60 cents per $100 here, and the clerk's fraud alert emails an owner within 24 hours of a new recording under their name.

faqs.a: Yes, for city operations on the county's 2026 chart, plus 0.2536 for city debt. All authorities total 19.9544 mills, or 20.3344 on the downtown development line.

faqs.q: Can a Miami landlord claim homestead?
faqs.a: No. The owner must live in the home as a permanent residence by January 1, and renting the unit ends the exemption.

faqs.q: What early payment discount does a Miami bill carry?
faqs.a: It steps down monthly from 4 percent for November to 1 percent for February. March is due at the full amount.

faqs.q: Does the Miami property appraiser collect tax?
faqs.a: No. Its home page says it neither sends bills nor sets or collects taxes. Payments go to the Miami-Dade Tax Collector.

faqs.q: How do I check my Miami taxable value?
faqs.a: Search by address, owner name or folio on the appraiser's site, or call 305-375-4712 to book an assessment review.
